chain.text: Mont Ventoux observatory runs a 60-cm reflector (2017) and a 20-cm outreach refractor, averaging 195 useful nights yearly (168 in 2024). Monthly data (~400 GB) transfers nightly to Marseille in 40 minutes. A new main camera (March 2025) has 30% lower read noise but needs an unapplied firmware update requiring one offline night. Past incidents: a 2023 dome-motor seizure bent a counterweight rod (replaced, limit switch added); a February 2025 timestamp offset lost three weeks of photometry (now GPS-checked each session). Rules: no observing during outreach evenings, raw frames compressed only after two years, and software changes need a test night. A proposed Spanish collaboration awaits evaluation of a shared scheduling tool and network capacity.

**Handover summary — Mont Ventoux Observatory**

60-cm reflector (2017) and 20-cm outreach refractor. Roughly 195 useful nights/year (168 in 2024; wet autumn). About 400 GB/night transfers to Marseille in 40 min. New main camera (March 2025) has ~30% lower read noise, but its firmware update is unapplied — needs one offline night. Incidents: 2023 dome-motor seizure bent a counterweight rod (replaced; limit switch added); Feb 2025 lost three weeks of photometry to an unnoticed 1.2 s timestamp offset — now GPS-checked each session. Rules: no observing during outreach evenings; raw frames compressed only after two years; software changes need a test night. Spanish collaboration (2025) awaits evaluation of a shared scheduling tool.

**Gap:** E13 — whether the network link can carry simultaneous transfers — is missing from this note.
